children: The European Central Bank is expected to leave interest rates unchanged later but its tone on France's fiscal issues and the prospect of future rate increases will determine the euro's reaction, ING's Francesco Pesole says in a note. Signalling that rates are likely to be raised in December would surprise markets, he says. "We see a slightly less committal message as more likely, perhaps that a December hike is possible or in play." However, the euro has shown it isn't ready to break below $1.1100 and the ECB is unlikely to trigger a major leg lower, he says. The euro falls 0.1% to $1.1144. The decision is at 1315 GMT followed by a press conference at 1345 GMT. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
